Date: Wed, 8 Nov 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Intro + RFP: pricing structure and migration economics

Jordan — thanks for the demo earlier this week. We're narrowing to two vendors and need a compact view of how Redwood would match/undercut our incumbent on list pricing while keeping parity on latency and feature support (streaming, function calls, KV cache).

Specifically would like: a price peg approach (one-line comparison), what onramp credits/credits-for-migration you can offer, and any technical constraints that would increase initial cost (e.g., dedicated pool minimums, egress).

Attached is our RFP + a quick cost model. Looking to present to procurement next Friday.

Regards,
Elena Voss
Head of Infrastructure Procurement
HelixAI

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Voss <elena.voss@helixai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Nov 2028 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + RFP: pricing structure and migration economics

Elena — thanks for sending. Initial summary below and attaching a compact price table so your team can slot numbers into the RFP. Happy to walk procurement through details.

High-level peg: we can offer a 15% effective price peg vs. your incumbent for 6 months on equivalent token spend, with a structured onramp that converts to a volume-step schedule after month 6. The peg assumes parity of throughput on our Dedicated tier (no additional latency premium).

Onramp & migration: up to $120k in migration credits applied as service credits (covers up to 60 hours of migration engineering + 3rd-party egress assistance). Additional professional services billed at our standard rate.

Constraints: dedicated pool minimum of 2 GPUs for predictable latency at >1.5M tokens/day. If Helix wants to start on shared-hosted, we can reduce the minimum but the peg becomes a 10% offset.

I've attached price_summary_v1.xlsx and included a short note on the dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs.

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Helix's RFP and my initial reply. Procurement will push hard on a 'price-peg' headline and want justification for credits in the model. Two asks: 1) can we increase the headline peg (to 20%) by shifting more value into time-limited credits vs list discount? 2) what's the realistic engineering hours we can justify for migration without eroding margin?

Key numbers in the attached calc (internal_migration_calculator.csv). If we do 20% peg for 3 months, we need to set an onboarding SLA and cap credits to protect us on slow migrations. Thoughts?

-JB

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Nov 2028 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helix RFP — need guidance on concession structure

Jordan — short answer: yes, we can present a 20% headline peg but structure it so the economics fall back to a 12–15% net OPEX reduction after credits expire. Recommendation:

- Headline: 20% price peg vs incumbent for first 90 days, limited to the first $1.2M of spend.
- Credits: $150k migration credit applied as one-time invoice credit; covers migration engineering (up to 80 hours) and a small egress stipend. Credits expire at day 120.
- Packaging: Starter Commitment — 3 months, then monthly step-down tiers at 10%/7%/5% based on trailing 90d consumption.
- Technical: Dedicated pool minimum stays at 2x A800-equivalent; we include a one-week performance tuning window (no additional charge) to hit parity. If load testing shows >30% extra engineering, we reserve right to escalate to PS.
- Exit clause: if Helix migrates off within first 6 months, credits convert to a clawback over the following invoice cycle.

This preserves margin while giving a strong procurement-friendly headline. I'll backfill with numbers for TCO impact.

—Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Nov 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helix RFP — pricing & packaging refinement

Adding packaging details to make this easy for procurement to accept:

- Offer: "Pilot Starter" — 3-month commitment at the 20% peg on first $400k; migration credit of $75k applied immediately on signing (reduces first invoice).
- Post-pilot: automatic conversion to a 12-month step plan with monthly check-ins and a one-time onboarding credit equal to 15% of the first-year committed spend if they commit within 30 days of pilot end.
- Ops: include 40 hours of free migration engineering as part of the Starter; beyond that PS rate applies. This hedges the risk Karthik called out.

If procurement asks for a bigger headline, counter with extending pilot length instead of increasing the peg.

Marissa
